title: JavaScript Standard Library Types knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a declaration file?
options: It proves a package is secure.
It describes the types of existing JavaScript APIs without providing their runtime implementation.
It replaces the runtime JavaScript implementation.
questions.answer_key: It describes the types of existing JavaScript APIs without providing their runtime implementation.
questions.explanation: Declaration files describe APIs and should be tested against real consumers and supported versions.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “JavaScript Standard Library Types”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with array and object types and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with array and object types and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Array and object types”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “JavaScript Standard Library Types”?
options: Check collections and iterators, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume promise and built-in object definitions is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check collections and iterators, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Collections and iterators”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
